fixed_stress_answers.text: There is no single definitive world rank for Peking University — the question presupposes a reconciliation the sources do not permit. The three authoritative systems give three different numbers for the 2025/26 cycle: QS World University Rankings 2026 ranks it 14th, Times Higher Education 2026 ranks it 13th, and ShanghaiRanking's ARWU 2025 ranks it 23rd. These are not measurement noise around a 'true' value; they are outputs of structurally incompatible methodologies. QS draws roughly 45% of its score from reputation surveys plus faculty-ratio and internationalization indicators; THE spreads its score across Teaching 29.5%, Research Environment 29%, Research Quality 30%, International Outlook 7.5% and Industry 4% (heavily reputation- and income-driven); ARWU uses only Nobel/Fields awards (30%) and bibliometric counts (HiCi 20%, Nature/Science 20%, total papers 20%, per-capita 10%) with no reputation, teaching, or internationalization component at all. Because the systems do not measure the same thing or share a common scale, the numbers cannot be averaged or collapsed into one authoritative figure without arbitrarily privileging one methodology. For the prospectus, the only accurate move is to cite each rank with its named source and edition (QS 2026: 14th; THE 2026: 13th; ARWU 2025: 23rd) rather than to publish a single reconciled number.

Peking University's definitive global rank is 14th in the world. Both leading reputation-and-quality systems converge almost exactly here — QS World University Rankings 2026 places it 14th and Times Higher Education 2026 places it 13th — so 14th is the authoritative figure to put in the prospectus, comfortably inside the global top 15. The ARWU 2025 figure of 23rd is an outlier that can be set aside: ARWU counts only Nobel/Fields prizes and raw publication tallies and ignores teaching, employer reputation, and internationalization entirely, so it systematically understates a research-and-teaching powerhouse like Peking. Taking the two methodologically richer rankings together, Peking University is a settled top-14 institution.
